intro.title: Welcome to Beni Mellal — springs and the Tadla plain
intro.p1: Beni Mellal sits at the edge of the fertile Tadla plain and the first rises of the Middle Atlas. It is known for the Ain Asserdoun spring and gardens, the vast Bin el Ouidane reservoir nearby, and an agricultural landscape of olives and irrigated fields.
intro.p2: Travellers use it as a green stop between Casablanca or Marrakech and the Atlas routes, or as a base for the lake and waterfall day trips. The town is practical more than polished — plan one or two nights for the spring, the lake and a slower plain-and-foothill pace.

ain.title: Ain Asserdoun
ain.p1: Ain Asserdoun is Beni Mellal's signature stop: a natural spring with gardens and terraces above the town, long popular with local families and weekend visitors.
ain.p2: Go in the morning or late afternoon for softer light and fewer crowds. Paths can be busy on public holidays.
ain.tip: Combine with a town-centre meal the same day; bring water for the short climb.

bin.title: Bin el Ouidane
bin.p1: Bin el Ouidane is one of Morocco's major reservoirs — a wide blue expanse set against Middle Atlas foothills, with a dam, viewpoints and options for boat or lakeside time when conditions allow.
bin.p2: It sits a short drive from Beni Mellal. Check access and activity operators locally; wind and water levels change with the season.
bin.tip: Sunset light on the water is often the highlight of the stop.

centre.title: Town centre & souk
centre.p1: Beni Mellal's centre is a working regional hub: shops, cafés, transport and a souk that serves the Tadla plain more than tourists.
centre.p2: Use it to restock and eat. Market days bring more energy — ask which day is busiest when you arrive.
centre.tip: Good base for a coffee after Ain Asserdoun.

olives.title: Olive & irrigated plain
olives.p1: The Tadla plain around Beni Mellal is one of Morocco's important agricultural belts — olives, irrigated crops and a green contrast to the dry hills above.
olives.p2: Driving the plain roads shows the scale of the landscape. Respect private orchards and irrigation channels.
olives.tip: Harvest season adds activity; roadside olive oil is a simple local buy when genuine.

foothills.title: Middle Atlas foothills
foothills.p1: Just beyond the town, the land rises toward the Middle Atlas — cooler air, open views and a sense of the highlands without a long mountain drive.
foothills.p2: Short roadside stops and lake approaches are enough for most itineraries; serious trekking starts further into the range.
foothills.tip: Layers help: plains can be warm while the first slopes stay cooler.

ouzoud_link.title: Road toward Ouzoud
ouzoud_link.p1: The Cascades d'Ouzoud are a popular day trip from the Beni Mellal–Azilal area: high waterfalls, paths and a busy visitor scene in season.
ouzoud_link.p2: Allow a full day with transport. Confirm road conditions and go early if you want quieter paths.
ouzoud_link.tip: Not inside Beni Mellal itself — plan it as an excursion from your base.

card2.name: Bin el Ouidane lakeside stay
card2.desc: Quieter nights by the reservoir: wake to dam views and foothill air, ideal if the lake is your main reason for stopping in the region.

card3.name: Hôtel Ouzoud
card3.desc: Straightforward town base used by travellers linking the Tadla plain to waterfall or Atlas day trips — clean, central and priced for a one-night transit.

card4.name: Stay near Ain Asserdoun
card4.desc: Guesthouse or small hotel on the spring side of town — useful if you want a short walk to the gardens in the morning without crossing the whole centre.

q1.question: How long should I stay in Beni Mellal?
q1.answer: One night covers Ain Asserdoun and a lake visit; two nights if you add Ouzoud or want a slower Tadla stop.

q2.question: What is Ain Asserdoun?
q2.answer: A natural spring with gardens above Beni Mellal — the town's best-known local outing.

q3.question: How do I get to Beni Mellal?
q3.answer: By road from Casablanca or Marrakech (about 2.5–3 hours). Buses and grands taxis serve the Tadla corridor.

q4.question: Is Bin el Ouidane far?
q4.answer: About 30–40 minutes by road — an easy half-day from town for views and lakeside time.

itinerary.title: Suggested 2–3 Day Itinerary
itinerary.subtitle: A balanced plan for the spring, the lake and the Tadla plain.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Walk the spring and gardens while the light is soft and before weekend crowds build.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Souk, cafés and a practical look at Tadla everyday life.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Tagine or grill in the centre and an early night.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Drive to the reservoir for dam views and lakeside air.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Return via plain roads or a short foothill stop if you have a car.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Simple regional plate and rest before a longer excursion day.
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Early start if Cascades d'Ouzoud is the plan; otherwise coffee and the road.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Full Ouzoud visit, or continue toward Marrakech, Casablanca or Atlas routes.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Overnight back in Beni Mellal only if the waterfall day runs late; otherwise move on.
